records.title: Land the pi-devs-psychologist appraiser: nested model call via ctx.modelRegistry.complete with completeSimple fallback, the English system prompt, the TypeBox appraisal schema (interventions max length 1, every claim cited to an evidence line), and the cadence/budget/single-flight policy

Land intervention policy, /psych report and persistence: at most one intervention delivered as a TUI note, steerAgent false by default so it never writes into the working agent's context, width-safe report, Trailing Space Contract completions, appendEntry persistence

Add the no-LLM codebase mapper slice: objective structural map (file sizes, slice layout, longest files, test-to-source ratio) so the appraiser reads a factual complexity figure instead of guessing; node:fs only, never reads outside cwd

Prior art for pi-devs-psychologist is dated in docs/inspiration.md: observer-model session summarisation exists (claude-mem, cognithor, engram, agent-memory-atlas) but only for memory; every 'developer psychologist' repo (reflog, gitblame-roast, coommitlore) is an offline git-stats persona roast. Live second-model appraisal of a working session against developer-psychology literature is uncovered

Land the pi-devs-psychologist observation kernel: git repo + VSA layout, session events to bounded observation window (prompts excluding extension-injected, tool calls paired by toolCallId, turns), arithmetic signal fold + evidence lines, heuristic lexicon, config cascade with model:'' as zero-spend default, statusline chip. 37/37 tests including a hand-counted fixture, tsc --noEmit exit 0

Fold the engine's own session entries into the psychologist's context: src/shared/history.ts reads sessionManager.getBranch() for operator cancellations (stopReason aborted), provider errors, output-limit cutoffs, model switches, thinking-level raises, compactions with the largest context that forced one, abandoned /tree branches, context removals vs rewrites, live /label bookmarks, declared session name, human wait times and prompt-cache read share. Refusals documented with reasons in docs/session-data.md and PRD 4.1: no message bodies, no system/skill sections, no reasoning text, no peer plugin custom entries, no cost totals, no cross-session history. 51/51 tests, tsc clean

Second role for the same observer: reviewer/pair programmer. Verified premise: edit args carry {path, edits:[{oldText,newText}]}, write args carry the whole content, and tool_execution_start.args reaches extensions verbatim, so the plugin already sees how work is done and keeps only path. Value is capability arbitrage: run the work on a model affordable in volume, the review on a stronger one at delivery boundaries. Must be a separate role with its own consent gate (psychologist = counts, reviewer = content that leaves the machine, never one switch). VSA shape in docs/adr/0001: slices/observer becomes a recorder with retain:'counts'|'content' (default counts) so one capture serves two projections. Not implemented on purpose: no content retention, no retain key. Tasks T12a-T12e

Model plan for this project: it will run multiple OpenRouter models for different roles, enabled by pi-openrouter-accounts which registers each account as its own provider id. Current accounts: openrouter-default (main) and openrouter-soukr (onlyFree). Mapping: worker on default, psychologist on soukr free tier (low cadence ~7 evidence lines fits a free tier, so the second opinion costs nothing extra and the work quota stays untouched), reviewer (T12) on default where capability pays. Rules recorded in docs/models.md: psychologist must not be the worker's model and a different account is not a different model; onlyFree rejects paid models at call time; evidence lines leave the machine so account choice is a data-policy decision too; budget isolation needs both maxAppraisalsPerSession and a separate account; account ids are never hardcoded in the plugin

Land the appraiser (T2-T4): one model call with stage-typed failures, the English rule-shaped prompt, the StringEnum appraisal contract with citation enforcement, and cadence/budget/single-flight policy. Found and fixed a silent bug: the load verdict uses field 'level' but the enforcement reader read 'state', so cognitive load could never be anything but unassessed forever; the schema test could not catch it, the enforcement test did. Also measured: extensions get ReadonlySessionManager with no appendUsage, so a background model call cannot be booked into session token/cost totals - the plugin reports its own spend instead. 119 tests, tsc clean
